nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph with vertices $s$ and $t$. A family $P_0, \dots, P_{n-1}$ of paths from $s$ to $t$ in $G$ is edge-disjoint when, for all indices $i \ne j$, no edge of $P_i$ is an edge of $P_j$.
nodes.title: Edge-disjoint paths

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph with vertices $s$ and $t$, and let $P_0, \dots, P_{n-1}$ be a family of paths from $s$ to $t$ in $G$, indexed by $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The family is internally vertex-disjoint when for all indices $i \ne j$, every vertex lying on both $P_i$ and $P_j$ is $s$ or $t$.
nodes.title: Internally vertex-disjoint paths

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices of $G$. A finite set $C$ of unordered pairs of vertices is an $s$-$t$ edge cut when every element of $C$ is an edge of $G$ and $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by deleting the edges in $C$.
nodes.title: Edge cuts separating two vertices

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, let $s$ and $t$ be vertices of $G$, and let $C$ be a set of vertices of $G$. Then $C$ is an $s$-$t$ vertex cut if and only if $s \notin C$, $t \notin C$, and every walk from $s$ to $t$ in $G$ passes through a vertex of $C$.
nodes.title: Vertex cuts are walk separators

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, let $s$ and $t$ be vertices of $G$, and let $C$ be a set of vertices of $G$. Then $C$ is an $s$-$t$ vertex cut when $s \notin C$, $t \notin C$, and $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in the graph obtained from $G$ by deleting every edge that has an endpoint in $C$.
nodes.title: Vertex cuts separating two vertices

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
